blocks.text: Jaws came back through the delivery doors with a piece of the fastening caught between his teeth.
Daniel pointed at the floor. The head spat it out.

Inside the annex, the temporary vault stood where Daniel had seen it that afternoon. The bank had closed, the workers had gone, and the room beyond the steel box was dark. Stacks of plasterboard waited beneath the scaffolding.
He set his canvas bag down and lifted out the Army ray.
Jaws drifted past his shoulder toward the vault’s wheel.
“Leave it,” Daniel said.
The head stopped, disappointed.

Daniel moved until he could see the vault’s roof, its right side and the clear space beneath its transport frame. No brickwork joined it to the annex. The whole thing had been brought here. The whole thing could leave.
He selected blue.
The beam touched the steel. Rivets drew closer together. The great wheel contracted, and the top of the vault sank below the scaffolding.
blocks.alt: Dork fires the blue shrink ray at the freestanding vault in the bank’s renovation annex.

blocks.text: Jaws followed it down, his eyes widening.
The frame dwindled with the box it supported. A dark rectangle of clean floor appeared around it, wider with every moment.
Daniel released the switch.
The vault stood beside his shoe.
For a second neither of them moved. Then Jaws bent low enough to bring one enormous iron tooth beside the tiny door.
Daniel scooped up the vault before he could test it.
An alarm began ringing.
He wrapped the steel box in a cloth, put it in his coat pocket and returned the ray to its bag. Jaws was already at the doors.
They left the alarm ringing behind them.
Laura had cleared the workshop floor as instructed.
The crates were stacked against the wall. A broad chalk rectangle lay between the bench and the parked tank, with room to walk around every side.
Daniel put the little vault in its center.
Laura looked from it to his face.
“That’s it?”
He stepped outside the chalk marks and raised the ray.
“Back.”
Jaws floated out of the rectangle. Laura moved beside the bench.
Red light crossed the concrete.
The little steel box rose past Daniel’s knees, then his waist. Its wheel spread wider than his hand. The frame settled against the floor with a deep, heavy sound.
Daniel switched the ray off.
The vault filled the cleared space.
blocks.alt: The restored vault towers over Dork, Laura and Jaws in the workshop, its door still closed.

blocks.text: He walked around it once. Every corner was where he had expected it to be. The door remained shut, its wheel level with his middle.
Jaws sailed around the other way and met him at the front.
“We took the whole thing.”
Daniel allowed himself a smile.
Laura stayed by the bench. From there she could see the thickness of the door’s outer edge, the massive hinges and the square metal lug beside the wheel.
She had asked him for something worth burning.
He had brought it home.
Daniel pulled the wheel.
It moved a little, then stopped against the locks. He tried it in the other direction with the same result.
Jaws pushed eagerly between him and the door.
“My turn.”
Daniel stepped aside.
The head opened wide and set his iron teeth around the projecting lug beside the wheel. His jaw closed with a hard clack.
He pulled.
blocks.alt: Jaws bites the projecting metal lug beside the vault’s wheel, leaving shallow gouges while the door stays shut.

blocks.text: A scrape ran through the workshop. Jaws twisted sideways, biting harder, his blond hair shaking with the effort.
The vault did not move.
Laura folded her arms inside her open coat. For the moment, both of them were watching the teeth.
Jaws let go, backed off and came at the lug from a different angle.
This time his lower teeth dragged along its edge. A small metal shaving fell to the floor.
He drew back to inspect his work.
Three bright gouges marked the steel. The lug remained attached. The door remained shut.
Daniel tried the wheel again.
Nothing.
Jaws hovered beside the damage, working his jaw slowly.
“Thick,” he said.
Laura nodded toward the tools along the wall.
“You’ve got a torch.”
Daniel looked at her.
She kept her attention on the vault.
“Worth trying before you burn through whatever’s inside.”
Daniel wheeled the cylinders over.
Laura moved the last loose papers away from the work area. She took her time, gathering a sheet that had slipped beneath a crate and smoothing it into the pile.
Behind her, the torch hissed.
Daniel had pulled on heavy gloves and lowered dark protective lenses over his spectacles. He brought the flame to the door’s right-hand seam, below the gouged lug.
Orange sparks struck the concrete.
blocks.alt: Dork uses a cutting torch on the vault’s door seam while Jaws watches from behind him.

blocks.text: Jaws watched from behind Daniel’s shoulder. After a while he drifted upward to see whether anything was happening at the top.
Nothing was.
The bright spot beneath the torch deepened into a narrow black groove. Daniel worked along it, stopped to inspect it, then went over the same short stretch again.
The workshop grew warm.
Laura sat on the edge of a stool with the papers beside her. She watched the groove and tried not to think about the scrap she had hidden after testing her plasma.
That thin piece had barely scorched.
This door was thicker than her wrist.
Daniel shut off the flame.
In the sudden quiet, a last spark clicked against the floor.
He raised the dark lenses and bent toward the seam. Soot marked the steel around a shallow cut. Beyond it, the door was solid.
Jaws lowered himself beside him.
Daniel put one gloved hand on the wheel and tried again.
It stopped in exactly the same place.
He turned toward Laura.
“Your turn.”
She got off the stool, leaving the papers behind.
Daniel held the unlit torch low, its tip pointed at the floor. He had made room for her in front of the door.
Jaws moved too. He floated just clear of the vault’s corner, looking at her with an eager grin.
Laura approached slowly.
The gouges shone beside the wheel. Below them, the torch mark ended before it had reached anything useful.
She leaned toward it without touching the hot steel.
Daniel waited.
Laura straightened and looked past him at the cylinders.
“Let it cool.”
“You’re going to heat it.”
“I want to see what I’m aiming at.”
She pointed at the soot, then folded her arms again before he could notice her fingers tightening.
Jaws turned to inspect the little groove. Daniel looked at her for another moment.
blocks.alt: Laura folds her arms as Dork waits with the unlit torch lowered; Jaws watches beside the still-sealed vault.

blocks.text: Then he set the torch in its holder.
“When it’s cool.”
Laura gave him a short nod.
She walked to the bench and picked up the pile of papers. There was nowhere else they needed to go. She carried them to a shelf anyway.
Behind her, Jaws tried the wheel once more.
The steel gave a dull clunk.
Daniel pulled a stool in front of the vault and sat down facing its door.
Laura put the papers on the shelf.
The three of them had brought an entire bank vault home.
Every dollar was still on the other side of the steel.
